headline: Phoenix wins a four-way opening week
dek: Four banners opened within 48 hours. Zenless Zone Zero's newcomer finished first in both Japan and China, Wuthering Waves doubled its month, and Honkai: Star Rail had its second-weakest month on record.
coverlines: Oct 21–22: Phoenix, Suoming, Akane Rin and Blade's rerun open together
Wuthering Waves doubles to ¥775M, its best month since May
Genshin is 4th in Japan but 1st on China's iPhone store
Si gives Endfield one of its best China openings so far
letter: October had a crowded opening week. On October 21 and 22, Zenless Zone Zero's Phoenix, Wuthering Waves' Suoming, Neverness to Everness's Akane Rin and Honkai: Star Rail's Mortenax Blade rerun all opened against each other. Over each banner's first seven days, Phoenix finished first in both markets: ¥222M in Japan against Suoming's ¥217M and Akane Rin's ¥151M, and $1.65M on China's iPhone store against $799K and $266K. Blade's rerun came fourth in both.

The month totals tell a different story. Wuthering Waves had September's Hsin still running, then added Suoming, and more than doubled to ¥775M, second only to Umamusume in Japan. Star Rail went the other way: after a huge September it fell 58%, to its second-weakest month in 43. Genshin was only fourth in Japan, but its Skirk rerun and the Vesna & Vodyanitsa banner kept it first on China's iPhone store at $6.35M.

Every game below has the month's banners with their Japan and China figures, the best daily chart rank each reached, and where each run sits in its game's history. For each new face there is a short note on who they are in the story.

wuwa.headline: Wuthering Waves doubles its month
wuwa.dek: Hsin's long run plus Suoming's arrival made October the game's best month since May.
body: Wuthering Waves took ¥775M in Japan in October, up 109% on September and second among the ten games tracked. It was also second on China's iPhone store, at $4.78M (+171%). The month ranks 5th of the 30 the game has had in Japan.

Hsin did most of the work. Her banner opened on September 30 and ran until October 22, earning ¥538M in Japan and $3.89M in China within October and peaking at #14 and #16. Suoming took over on the 22nd. In ten days she added ¥248M and $896K, and her #11 in Japan was the best rank either banner reached all month.
wuwa.pull: Suoming's #11 was the best Japan rank Wuthering Waves reached all month.

hsr.headline: Star Rail comes down after a huge September
hsr.dek: Pearl carried the month while Mortenax Blade's rerun barely registered.
body: Honkai: Star Rail made ¥671M in Japan, down 58% from a very strong September. It was still third among the games tracked, but it was the game's second-weakest month of the 43 we have. In China it fell 63%, to $1.97M.

Pearl, who opened on September 28, earned ¥531M of that, peaking at #17 in Japan and #46 in China. The Mortenax Blade rerun opened in the same week as Phoenix and Suoming and took ¥82M, peaking at #52. By total revenue it ranks 63rd of the game's 64 banners.

genshin.headline: Genshin: fourth in Japan, first in China
genshin.dek: A quiet month in Japan. On China's iPhone store, no game earned more.
body: Genshin Impact made ¥424M in Japan, down 32% and 30th of its 34 months on game-i's monthly series. China told the opposite story: at $6.35M Genshin was the top earner on China's iPhone store.

Two banners split the month almost evenly. The Skirk rerun opened on October 13 and earned ¥211M in Japan and $3.31M in China, peaking at #43 and #22. Vesna & Vodyanitsa added ¥209M and $3.04M. In Japan, Skirk's rerun ranks 104th of the 107 Genshin banners tracked.

zzz.headline: Phoenix rises
zzz.dek: ZZZ's 3.3 headliner won October's four-way opening week in both markets.
body: Zenless Zone Zero made ¥414M in Japan in October (+9.5%) and $2.14M on China's iPhone store (+60%). It finished fifth in both markets.

Phoenix opened on October 21 and earned ¥268M in Japan and $1.81M in China in her first eleven days. She peaked at #10 in Japan and #19 in China, the best ranks of any banner that opened that week. Her run already ranks 25th of ZZZ's 40 banners in Japan and 12th in China, and it runs until November 11. Roxy, whose banner opened on September 30, added ¥142M before handing over.
zzz.pull: Phoenix's #10 was the best rank of any banner that opened in the October 21–22 week.

nte.headline: NTE rocks into its half-anniversary
nte.dek: Akane Rin's debut arrived with NTE's half-year anniversary on October 21.
body: Neverness to Everness made ¥379M in Japan, up 24% on September, and $770K on China's iPhone store. These figures only cover mobile stores. Perfect World says about 60% of NTE's spending comes through PC and its own Android client, which this data can't see.

Blackbird's banner from September 30 earned ¥222M. Akane Rin opened with the anniversary and took ¥180M in eleven days, peaking at #19 in Japan and #85 in China. In Japan her run so far ranks 9th of NTE's 10 banners.

endfield.headline: Si gives Endfield one of its best China openings
endfield.dek: She was only mid-table in Japan, but on China's iPhone store Si's run is already among the game's best.
body: Arknights: Endfield made ¥288M in Japan (−4.3%). On China's iPhone store it rose 40% to $2.15M, fourth among the nine games tracked there.

Si opened on October 15 and earned ¥239M in Japan and $1.99M in China, peaking at #15 and #13. In China her run already ranks 4th of Endfield's 15 banners; in Japan it is 9th. Tangtang's rerun followed on October 29.
